newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol hopes for upstream Iraq oil deal - source.
newsitem.headline: Repsol hopes for upstream Iraq oil deal - source.

text.p: Repsol is to meet Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Mohammed Rasheed on Tuesday in talks which the Spanish firm hopes will eventually lead to a similar upstream oilfield development deal as one secured by Russia in March, an industry source said.

"Russia already has a contract signed with Iraq which will come into effect if or when the embargo is lifted, and Repsol would like something similar. There'll be some kind of contact between (Repsol and the Iraqi minister) over the course of the day," the source told Reuters.
Repsol wants access to reserves of two billion barrels of crude in the Nasiriyah field in central Iraq, which represents roughly 10 percent of world oil reserves, the source said.
The Iraqi Minister is due to give at press conference in Madrid at 1500 GMT today.
However, the dource said talks were at an early stage.

"The context of Rasheed's visit is not that it's a specific visit to sign anything. He's simply attempting to continue the process of lessening, or lifting altogether, the oil embargo," the source said.
"Repsol has a specific interest in Iraq, where it has no presence. What we don't know is whether they'll be awarded a contract," the source said.
Russia signed a deal with Baghdad in March to develop Iraq's Qurana oilfield. Russian officials have said that no work will be begun on the ground until U.N. sanctions have been lifted.
United Nations sanctions were imposed against Iraq in 1990 after its invasion of Kuwait.
Late on Monday, the U.N.Security Council adopted a resolution threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it does not allow arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.
